translation.text: These and all the others with them took wives for themselves, and each chose one for himself. Then they began to go in to them and join themselves to them.[a] They taught them charms and incantations,[b] the cutting of roots, and made them acquainted with plants.[c]

“These” is parenthesized and the first conjunction bracketed in the selected Charles printing. The joining verb and magical terms have variants; the source is not harmonized to another language witness. “Plants” includes the plants/shrubs sense discussed in the printed apparatus.

translation.text: They devoured all the fruit of human labor, until people were unable to feed them.[a][b]

lexical_decisions.rationale: The clause begins with a relative form, literally resembling “those who ate,” but in context it continues the description of the preceding beings. “They” supplies natural English continuity, while “devoured” conveys voracious consumption without adding imagery absent from the verb.

translation.text: And as humankind was being destroyed, they cried out, and their voice reached heaven.[a]

footnotes.text: Literally, “in the destruction of humankind.” The phrase may also be rendered, “as people were perishing.”

lexical_decisions.rationale: The prepositional phrase is formally “in the destruction of humankind.” In context, English naturally expresses the circumstance temporally (“as”), while the passive wording preserves the source’s image of human destruction without specifying an agent not named here. “Humankind” represents collective ሰብእ without restricting the reference to adult males.
